action: Vanderbilt students and staff: follow university instructions before reconnecting devices, change passwords when asked, and watch for phishing that references the incident.
date_note: Incident began Nov 9; this entry reflects recovery reporting on Nov 13
exec: A major research university is operating with restricted systems; the data-theft claim is unverified but would be large if true.
impact: Most systems and applications were available again by the 19 November update; OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams remained disabled.
plain: Vanderbilt University shut down many computer systems after a ransomware attack. A criminal group claims it stole a million people's details; the university has not confirmed that.
summary: Vanderbilt told students and staff on November 9 to shut down university devices during an active cybersecurity incident. Its 19 November update says most systems and applications are available, while OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams stay disabled. The BYOD group claims it took more than 1 million Social Security numbers; the university has not confirmed this. A former student has filed a proposed class action; its allegations are untested.
title: Vanderbilt University restricts systems after ransomware attack; BYOD group claims 1 million records

validation.note: University updates page (6 p.m. Nov. 19), Government Technology and Beinsure read; the theft claim and the lawsuit allegations are unconfirmed by the university or a court.

review.note: Compared Nov 9 start, restricted systems, BYOD 1M SSN claim unconfirmed, lawsuit in M.D. Tenn. against GovTech, Beinsure, SharkStriker
